saints.name: St. Cuthbert
saints.title: Bishop of Lindisfarne
saints.shortBlurb: The shepherd turned monk of Lindisfarne, beloved wonderworker of Northumbria and lover of solitude…
biography: Born about 634 in the border country, Cuthbert was a shepherd on the hills near Melrose when, on the night in 651 that St. Aidan of Lindisfarne died, he saw in vision a soul borne to heaven by angels; soon after he entered the monastery of Melrose under the prior Boisil.

Made prior of Melrose and then, after the Synod of Whitby, of Lindisfarne, he journeyed tirelessly among the villages of Northumbria, winning the name of wonder-worker of Britain. Yet he yearned for solitude, and in 676 withdrew to the bare island of Inner Farne.

Elected bishop in 684 and consecrated at York by Archbishop Theodore in 685 — exchanging Hexham for Lindisfarne — he resigned within two years and died on Inner Farne on 20 March 687. His body, found incorrupt in 698, rests at Durham, and Bede wrote his life in verse and prose. He is the beloved patron of Northumbria.
saints.knownFor: His missionary charity and holiness in Northumbria.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 20 March
